tweets.text:
Here's my analogy for Elysium:

Imagine someone is exploring a desert in the middle of California.

They think "Man, California is a really popular state and a lot of people live in some of the big cities... imagine if this desert had water. Well, I'm sure people would move out here! And if they wanted to move out here, there would definitely need to be some roads... so I'll build the roads to the desert just in case there's ever water because then people would definitely want to build businesses... why? Because the desert is in California! So there'd obviously be a need for it."

So that person then creates a sales deck for a new community smack dab in the middle of the desert. They pitch the idea that there's enough growth elsewhere in the state that most likely they'll probably eventually find water, and it makes sense to a lot of people... because people in California like California.

And the cool part? The land in the new community is still so dang cheap! And the rest of the state is so expensive that when the people come out there, it's probably gonna boom.

So they buy the cheap land, and start building businesses because there were roads to get there.

And while the businesses are being built the community IS booming.

The people that bought the land struck gold!

Then slowly but surely, the building stops... and the people that were building have no reason to be there anymore because their job is finished... and then, nobody is left in the community.

Why?

Because they built it before they ever found the water.

They built it in anticipation that one day they might.

And that was enough for a bit... but at the end of the day, they're still in a desert and nobody is going to go out there unless there's an actual need to do it.

So, the roads still exist.

The empty buildings still exist.

But they slowly decay until people forget they ever did.
